names.official: Independent State of Papua New Guinea

summary: Papua New Guinea gives a visa on arrival to a short list of countries — including the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel and much of the Pacific — whose citizens can instead apply online in advance for a 60-day Easy Visitor Permit (no visa fee, USD 50 eVisa fee). Other nationalities apply for a visitor visa on the paper form before travel. Melanesian Spearhead Group neighbors get a 30-day visa on arrival.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival and have at least one blank page for the visa label and entry stamp.

Papua New Guinea Immigration and Citizenship Authority

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required for travelers aged one year and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including those who only transited through the airport of such a country, however short the transit.

source.name: World Health Organization — International Travel and Health, Annex 1 (18 November 2022, revised 3 January 2023)

vaccinations.name: Hepatitis A, typhoid and tetanus
vaccinations.text: Not required for entry, but widely recommended for PNG along with up-to-date routine vaccinations. Malaria is present across most of the country below 1,800 m — discuss prophylaxis with a travel clinic well before departure.

source.name: Papua New Guinea Immigration and Citizenship Authority

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not a condition of entry, but medical care outside Port Moresby is very limited and serious cases are evacuated to Australia at high cost — comprehensive coverage with medical evacuation is strongly advised.

source.name: Papua New Guinea Immigration and Citizenship Authority

onwardTicket.text: Tourist eVisa holders must hold a confirmed onward or return ticket, and airlines check it at check-in along with the visa approval.

source.name: PNG Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority — Visa Information Guide

proofOfFunds.text: eVisa applicants are asked to show sufficient funds for the visit, typically through recent bank statements, plus an itinerary and accommodation or tour bookings. No fixed figure is published.

source.name: PNG Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority — Visa Information Guide

declarations.name: PNG Digital Arrival Card (PNGDAC)
declarations.submitWindow: Online within 72 hours before arrival, and before check-in
declarations.text: Every traveller, including PNG citizens and permanent residents, must complete the free PNG Digital Arrival Card online before arrival. It replaced the paper incoming passenger card from 1 October 2025, and since August 2026 airlines must not issue a boarding pass without it. Show the confirmation with your passport on arrival. It is not a visa.

source.name: PNG Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority — Mandatory completion of PNG Digital Arrival Card

currencyLimits.text: Amounts of PGK 20,000 or more, or the foreign-currency equivalent, must be declared to customs on arrival and departure. Larger transfers out of the country may need Bank of Papua New Guinea approval.

source.name: Papua New Guinea Immigration and Citizenship Authority

notes: Firearms, ammunition and offensive weapons are prohibited without prior authorization.
Quarantine rules cover fresh food, seeds, plants, wooden artefacts and animal products — carved souvenirs may need treatment or a permit to take home.
Cultural artefacts and anything made from protected wildlife, including bird of paradise plumes, cannot be exported without a permit.

payments.text: Cards work in Port Moresby hotels, larger supermarkets and some resorts, but almost nowhere else. ATMs are concentrated in the towns and can be unsafe to use after dark. Carry kina in cash and keep it out of sight.

safety.text: Crime is a genuine concern, especially in Port Moresby and Lae, where carjacking, robbery and opportunistic street crime occur. Most visitors travel with pre-arranged transfers, avoid walking after dark, and stay clear of highlands areas affected by tribal violence. Rural and resort areas are generally calmer.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Papua New Guinea travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the dry season — the window for the Kokoda Track, highlands festivals such as the Goroka and Mount Hagen shows, and reliable domestic flights.

idp.text: Papua New Guinea is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Geneva, 1949), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3)

driving.text: Papua New Guinea is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Papua New Guinea yet.

tips.text: Arrange an airport transfer with your hotel before you land, do not walk in Port Moresby or Lae — including short distances in daylight — and keep car doors locked in traffic. Most incidents involving visitors happen on foot or at ATMs.

If your nationality is on ICA's visa-on-arrival list, you can apply for the Easy Visitor Permit on the official portal at evisa.ica.gov.pg at least two weeks out; ICA's turnaround is up to 10 working days. Everyone else needs a visitor visa before flying, applied for on the paper form, so allow several weeks.
Malaria is present nearly everywhere below 1,800 m and dengue occurs too. Start prophylaxis before you arrive, use repellent from dusk, and sleep under a net outside air-conditioned hotels.

There is no road network linking most of the country — Air Niugini and PNG Air domestic flights are the only practical way between regions, they fill up around festival dates, and delays are routine. Leave a buffer day before your international flight home.

Land and custom matter: ask permission before entering villages, photographing people or walking on clan land, and expect to pay a small fee for access to sites and trails. A local guide is both good manners and good security.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: Yes, every foreign visitor needs a visa. Citizens of the countries on ICA's visa-on-arrival list — including the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel and much of the Pacific — can get one at Port Moresby's airport, and Fijian, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu citizens get a 30-day visa on arrival. The same visa-on-arrival nationalities can apply online in advance for the 60-day Easy Visitor Permit (no visa fee, USD 50 eVisa fee); everyone else — including US, Australian, New Zealand and EU citizens — applies for a visitor visa on the paper form before travel.

faq.question: How do I apply for the PNG tourist eVisa?
faq.answer: The eVisa portal (evisa.ica.gov.pg) is for citizens of countries on ICA's visa-on-arrival list. Apply there with a passport scan, photo, itinerary, accommodation details, onward ticket and proof of funds; ICA's turnaround is up to 10 working days, and you carry the approval with you to check-in. Other nationalities use the paper visitor-visa form.

faq.question: Is there a visa on arrival in Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: Yes, for the countries on the visa-on-arrival list published by the Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority, at Jacksons International Airport in Port Moresby. The list includes the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and most Pacific Island states; mainland New Zealand, France and the United States are not eligible. Chinese ordinary passport holders qualify only in an organized tour group. Check the list before you fly.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: The tourist eVisa allows up to 60 days per entry. Extensions are possible from inside the country through the Immigration and Citizenship Authority, but apply well before the visa expires — overstaying carries fines and removal.

faq.question: Is Papua New Guinea safe to visit?
faq.answer: It needs care rather than avoidance. Port Moresby and Lae have significant crime and parts of the highlands see tribal violence, so travelers use pre-arranged transport, avoid moving around after dark and often travel with a guide or operator. Dive resorts, Milne Bay, Tufi and the Sepik are generally calmer.

faq.question: What vaccinations do I need for Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you arrive from, or transited through the airport of, a yellow fever risk country. Beyond that nothing is compulsory, but hepatitis A, typhoid and tetanus are commonly recommended, and malaria prophylaxis is important for almost all of the country.
